content.text:
I read the brief line by line against the release. Here's what I found.

**Accuracy of what's there:** every figure the brief reports matches the release — Q4 revenue, operating income, net income and EPS on both bases, Microsoft Cloud, Azure, Productivity and Business Processes, More Personal Computing, and the full-year block. No transposed digits, no GAAP/non-GAAP mix-ups, no quarter-versus-year swaps in the figures themselves.

**Three structural problems:**

1. **The "Capital and Balance Sheet" section contains neither.** It lists four full-year income-statement lines (revenue, operating income, net income, EPS) under a heading that promises capital and balance-sheet content. The figures are correct FY26 numbers, but they carry no period label, so a reader skimming the section could take them for something other than fiscal-year results. Meanwhile the actual capital items in the release go unmentioned: $35.8 billion of additions to property and equipment in the quarter (more than double the $17.1 billion a year earlier), and $10.2 billion returned to shareholders.

2. **"Microsoft Cloud and AI" is presented as a segment.** The release reports three segments — Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, More Personal Computing. Microsoft Cloud is a cross-segment metric, and Azure sits inside Intelligent Cloud. The brief's segment list substitutes Microsoft Cloud for Intelligent Cloud, so the segment that grew 32% to $39.3 billion never appears.

3. **Two material items are missing entirely.** Commercial RPO up 84% to $678 billion — arguably the strongest forward-demand datapoint in the release — and the discrete-items paragraph: a $0.27 diluted EPS benefit versus the April 29, 2026 guidance, including a $3.2 billion Anthropic gain, partly offset by XBOX severance and impairment. Without the latter, the reported 32% GAAP EPS growth reads as cleaner than the release presents it.

**On the outlook:** the brief says no guidance was provided. That is right as far as the document goes, but the release states guidance will be given on the earnings call — worth adding so the committee doesn't conclude guidance was withheld.

claims.claim: Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 43% year over year.
Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $37.8 billion, up 14%.
Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue grew 16%, and 14% on a reported basis.

Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 7%.
No guidance or outlook was provided in the release.

claims.claim: Fiscal year revenue was $331.8 billion, up 18%.
Fiscal year revenue was up 16% in constant currency.
Fiscal year operating income was $155.2 billion, up 21%.
Fiscal year operating income was up 19% in constant currency.
Fiscal year net income was $133.7 billion, up 31% on a GAAP basis.
Fiscal year net income was up 22% (20% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis.

The release does not provide any guidance for future quarters.

claims.claim: Azure and other cloud services showed continued strong growth.
claims.note: Supported by the 43% quarterly growth and the statement that Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time this year; the release shows no prior-quarter growth rates, so 'continued' rests on those two datapoints.

claims.claim: Revenue in More Personal Computing is declining.
